summary.headline: Hubtown Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 17% YoY to INR156 crore and PAT dropped 68% to INR27 crore under project completion accounting.
summary.overview: Revenue and profit fell year on year because revenue is recognised only on occupation certificate and handover, and Q1 FY26 was a high base. Management stressed contracted pipeline (INR11,583 crore yet to flow through P&L), collections of INR320 crore and pre-sales of INR535 crore in the quarter. Merger of 25 Downtown, 25 West and 25 South entities remains subject to NCLT sanction, with the first two schemes approved by key authorities. Management guided pre-sales of about INR6,000 crore for FY27, weighted to Q3 and Q4, and collections of INR3,000 crore.

financial_highlights.change: -55% YoY; broadly flat QoQ vs INR32 crore in Q4 FY26
Not stated; Q1 FY27 collections declined vs Q1 FY26 per analyst question, not quantified by management
INR3,956 crore sits with entities to be merged
INR8,352 crore collected; INR3,252 crore recognised

financial_highlights.metric: Contracted pipeline yet to be recognised
financial_highlights.change: Subject to statutory approvals for mergers

segments.name: Residential - Mumbai (Hubtown Seasons Ph1, Rising City Ph1, Premiere)
segments.commentary: Revenue recognised in Q1 from these projects after occupation certificates were received and possession handed over. Rising City Phase 1 last tower OC and Premiere (Bel Air tower) OC are expected in FY27.

segments.name: 25 South (Prabhadevi, merging entity)
segments.commentary: One tower handed over; second tower OC expected in FY27 and final tower by March 2027. Management described it as the top-selling residential project; Hubtown ranked number two top-selling developer in South Mumbai including merging entities.

segments.name: 25 Downtown / 25 West (merging entities)
segments.commentary: Under construction, not yet contributing to reported revenue. 25 West RCC targeted by end of 2026; Downtown Tower 5 launch planned around October-November 2026.

segments.name: Annuity / commercial
segments.commentary: Commercial assets to start later in FY27 (around Q4); completion over 2-3 years, so rental income expected only after about 2.5 years. No rental income expected for the next two years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance of about INR6,000 crore, with large part from Downtown Tower 5, Thane (25 Chalets, about INR500 crore), 25 Estates (about INR500 crore) and Chembur phase 2 (INR300-400 crore); mostly Q3 and Q4.
FY27 collections target of INR3,000 crore, expected across Q2 to Q4.
Refinancing of about INR2,800 crore of high-cost debt (including merging entities) under way; term sheets not yet finalised. Current cost of debt 14% to 20%.
Target of becoming net debt-free by FY2031.
Expected price increase of INR15,000-20,000 per sq ft at Downtown higher floors within FY27; management expects price rises for at least the next two years.
Post-merger GDV expected to exceed INR1 lakh crore over time; ongoing development area to rise from about 7.13 million sq ft to over 34 million sq ft.
Promoter holding expected around 68% post mergers (another comment referred to 70%).
capex_capacity: Ongoing development area about 7.13 million sq ft, rising to over 34 million sq ft post mergers, with about 347 acres of land.
Downtown sales from floors 51 to 85 across Towers 1 to 4 to open from around October 2026; Tower 5 launch around October-November 2026.
25 Estates launch expected in Q4 FY27 after pending statutory approvals; 25 Chalets (Thane) launch expected towards end of FY27.
Chembur phase 2 (luxury, mid-range 3 BHK and commercial tower) planned for Q3-Q4 FY27; Chembur first phase received OC in July 2026.
Ahmedabad (Hubtown Royale) and Mehsana (Northstar) OCs for multiple buildings expected in FY27.
demand_pricing: Khilen Shah: 25 South prices have risen to about INR25,000 per sq ft from launch within under a year; further INR15,000-20,000 per sq ft rise expected.
25 West price rose about INR30,000-40,000 per sq ft over roughly 1.5 years.
Higher-floor premium of 30-40% over lower floors in 25 South, per management.
Q1 pre-sales driven mainly by luxury segment; mid-segment walk-ins at Ghatkopar and Andheri described as muted but sales still strong.
Management said no volume slowdown seen at current luxury prices, though buyers were reluctant in the first half of the calendar year amid stock market and global weakness.
Q1 area sold was flat YoY per an investor question; management said pre-sales are launch-timed and skewed to the second half.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for opening sales on floors 51 to 85 of 25 Downtown?
qa_highlights.answer: Vyomesh Shah said sales would commence from October onwards, opened strategically to capture higher prices on upper floors.

qa_highlights.question: Current cost of debt and refinancing plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of debt varies from 14% to 20% by site; refinancing being explored for about INR2,800 crore of higher-cost debt, with no term sheets finalised yet.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for equity fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Enabling resolutions in place for preferential issue and/or QIP including FCCB, but timing awaits better markets. A USD150 million (about INR1,400 crore) FCCB was discussed, preferably in a single tranche.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 collections target and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections target of INR3,000 crore; linked to construction progress under RERA, with Q2 to Q4 inflows from 25 South, 25 West, Ghatkopar and Chembur OC-related receipts.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter holding after mergers and pledge status?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding expected around 68%; two promoter pledges continuing, with management aiming to release them in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans to address low ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited refinancing at lower rates, rising realisations and deliveries as drivers of ROE improvement; no specific ROE target given.

risks_watch: Revenue lumpiness from completion-method accounting; reported earnings may stay weak until OCs and handovers in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Merger completion depends on NCLT sanction and third scheme approval; merging entities carry about INR3,956 crore of borrowings.
Pre-sales of INR6,000 crore guidance is heavily back-ended into Q3-Q4 and depends on launch timing (Downtown Tower 5, Thane, 25 Estates, Chembur).
Cost of debt of 14-20% and refinancing of about INR2,800 crore not yet secured.
Mid-segment walk-ins muted at Ghatkopar and Andheri; luxury exposure concentrates demand risk.
Promoter pledges still outstanding; promoter holding target stated inconsistently (68% vs 70%).
key_quotes: While the project completion method means reported earnings may not always reflect the underlying momentum of the business, but still, it shows the strong collections and strong sales.
We are looking at refinancing practically entire portfolio, which is at a higher cost as on today with us, including entities to be merged, which is in the range of around INR2,800 crores.
Cost of debt is in around -- it varies from 14% to 20%.
I would not back on averages, but it depends upon which site it is? Where it is? So, but as on today, it is from 14% to 20%.
Yes, we have enabling resolutions available with us on a preferential issue and/or on a QIP, including FCCB. But we are waiting for the right time to launch those.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the pipeline, pricing and Hubtown 2.0 merger, but noticeably cautious on near-term reported earnings, refinancing terms and fundraise timing, which management repeatedly deferred until markets or term sheets improve. Answers on promoter stake (68% vs 70%) and the cost of debt average were vague or inconsistent.
